title: Intelligence Systems Integration and Maintenance Technician (IS Intg/Maint Tech)
raw_text:
8-353. MOS 353T—Intelligence Systems Integration and Maintenance Technician (IS Intg/Maint Tech)
    a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
    b. Prerequisites. DA Pam 611-21.
    c. MOS 353T. MOS 353T is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOS is 35T.
    d. Associated SQI.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 7--Parachutist.
         (3) 8--Instructor.
         (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
         (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
    e. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all warrant officer
MOS).
          (1) Q1--Interactive On-Net Operator (Personnel Only).
          (2) Q3--Cryptologic Cyber Analyst (Personnel Only).
    f. Qualifications.
         (1) WO1/CW2 must--
               (a) Be a U.S. citizen.
               (b) Possess a security eligibility of TOP SECRET with eligibility for access to sensitive
compartmented information (SCI).
               (c) Complete the Intelligence Systems Integration and Maintenance Technician MI Warrant Officer
Basic Course (WOBC).
               (d) SEC + and NET + certifications are desired.
         (2) CW3 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1).
               (b) Complete the resident MI Warrant Officer Advanced Course (WOAC).
         (3) CW4 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(2).
               (b) Complete Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE).
         (4) CW5 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(3).
               (b) Complete Warrant Officer Senior Service Education (WOSSE).
    g. Duties.
         (1) WO1/CW2 --
               (a) Provides technical guidance and advice to commanders and staff on the management and
utilization of the Army and Joint Forces Military Intelligence /Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance
(MI/ISR) systems and networks.
               (b) Oversees shop operations and facility work flow for both ground and airborne ISR systems.
               (c) Serves as principal advisor to the Command and staff on intelligence maintenance operations,
training, policies, and procedures.
               (d) Employs external capabilities, and integrates automation ISO intelligence maintenance
operations.
               (e) Conducts all intelligence maintenance operations IAW applicable laws, policies.
               (f) May serve as a Discipline Analyst or Functional Manager at any echelon.
         (2) CW3 --
               (a) Directs and performs duties described in paragraph g(1).
               (b) Advises senior staff members, decision, and policy makers on intelligence maintenance
operations, training, policies, and procedures.
               (c) Directs and conducts intelligence maintenance coordination with Joint, Interagency,
Intergovernmental, and Multinational partners.
               (d) Develops and plans all intelligence maintenance operations.
               (e) May serve as Maintenance Shop OIC.
               (f) May serve as a Discipline Collection Manager at any echelon.
               (g) May serve as an OC/T at a CTC or MCTP.
               (h) May serve as a Doctrine Writer.
               (i) May serve as a Detachment Commander.
               (j) May serve as an instructor at the WOCC, or at 111th MI BDE.
                (k) May serve on the Joint or Combined Staff.
               (l) May serve as a Doctrine or Capabilities Developer.
         (3) CW4--
                (a) Manages, directs and performs duties described in paragraph g(1) and g(2).
                (b) Serves as the principal advisor to senior staff members, decision, and policy makers on
intelligence maintenance operations, training, policies, and procedures.
                (c) Directs and conducts intelligence maintenance coordination with Joint, Interagency,
Intergovernmental, and Multinational partners.
               (e) May serve as a Discipline Collection Manager at any echelon.
               (f) May serve as an OC/T at a CTC or MCTP.
               (g) May serve as a Doctrine Writer.
               (h) May serve as an instructor at the WOCC, or at 111th MI BDE.
               (i) May serve on the Joint or Combined Staff.
               (j) May serve as a Doctrine or Capabilities Developer.
               (k) May serve as the HRC MI WO Assignments Manager.
         (4) CW5 --
               (a) MI CW5s are proficient in the duties described in the duties paragraphs of one or
more MI WO MOSs.
               (b) MI CW5s are branch technical experts and master-level technical and tactical
experts who perform the primary duties of technical leader, manager, multidiscipline intelligence
integrator, and advisor.
               (c) Provide direction, guidance, resources, assistance, and supervision necessary for
subordinates to perform their duties.
               (d) Provide leader development, talent and lifecycle management, mentorship, advice,
and counsel to enlisted Soldiers, warrant officers, and branch officers and have special warrant
officer leadership and representation responsibilities within their respective commands
               (e) Primarily support division, corps, echelons above corps, and major command
operations.
               (f) Advise commanders and branch assignment managers on the assignments and
placement of Military Intelligence warrant officers world-wide.
               (g) Provide essential advice to commanders on warrant officer issues and perform
other officer level duties as required consistent with senior staff officer responsibilities.
               (h) May serve as the Senior WO advisor in MOS immaterial (011A) billets based on
technical knowledge and understanding of Army and Joint doctrine.
               (i) May serve on the Army Staff
               (j) May serve as a Capabilities Branch Chief
               (k) May serve as the MI WO Proponent
               (l) May serve as the CCWO of the MI Branch
               (m) MI Senior Field Grade Warrant Officers must have competed the WO Senior
Service Education Course prior to nomination for specified CW5 billets.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
         (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
         (2) Have normal color discrimination with corrected vision per one of the following three categories of the
good eye, bad eye categories: 20/40-20/70; 20/30-20/100; 20/20-20/400.
        (3) Have hearing wherein sound amplitude in one ear does not exceed 45 decibels at frequencies 250,
         (4) Have hearing wherein sound amplitude in one ear does not exceed 45 decibels at frequencies 250,
500, 1000 and 2000 CPS (HZ) or 65 decibels at frequency 4000.
         (5) Qualifying Scores
         A minimum OPAT score of Long Jump (LJ) – 120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT) – 350 cm,
Strength Deadlift (SD) – 120 lbs, and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 36 shuttles in Physical Demands
Category “Moderate” (Gold).
         (6) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill
levels: W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The
grades are listed in the following standards of grade tables:
              (a) Table 8-353T-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
              (b) Table 8-353T-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
